$comment: Canonical catalog of the 7 Sorrows of Mary (Servite Rosary/Chaplet of Our Lady of Sorrows), in order. imageKey doubles as the lookup key into MysteryTranslations (title/fruit/description per language, reusing the same imageKey-keyed lookup Franciscan Crown's Adoration of the Magi uses — see mysteries.json) and the filename stem under Shared/Images/{imageKey}. Unlike Franciscan Crown, none of the 7 reuse an existing Rosary mystery imageKey — only the Crucifixion sorrow thematically overlaps sorrowful_05_crucifixion, but is traditionally illustrated/meditated distinctly here (Mary's own vantage at the foot of the Cross, John 19:25-27, not the moment of Jesus's death, Luke 23:44-46, used for sorrowful_05_crucifixion). Source of truth: iOS's Models/SevenSorrowsCatalog.swift (this file was built from it); Android's models/SevenSorrowsCatalog.kt and Windows's Models/SevenSorrowsCatalog.cs must carry the exact same set/order. Keep in sync — see README.md in this directory.

images.note: All 7 sorrow images currently point at a generic placeholder graphic (deep wine-red cross on a rose-tan background), not real artwork — real public-domain art with proper attribution has not been sourced yet. See each platform's About screen, which labels these explicitly as 'artwork pending' rather than citing fake attributions.

languages.note: ar/he/ru/tl fall back to Latin via the standard translation-dispatcher fallback (same mechanism as any missing content-layer entry) until dedicated translations are added in a later pass.

sorrows.title: The Loss of the Child Jesus in the Temple
Mary Meets Jesus on the Way of the Cross
sorrows.note: The one sorrow with no direct Gospel citation — a traditional devotional scene (the same status as the Stations of the Cross's 4th station), not a quoted verse.

sorrows.title: Mary at the Foot of the Cross
Mary Receives the Body of Jesus

closing.$comment: 3 Hail Marys for Our Lady's tears, then a fixed versicle/response/collect — unlike the Rosary/Franciscan Crown, this closing is not a user choice (no Marian-antiphon picker); it's the Servite Chaplet's own traditional close. See content-keys.json's sevenSorrowsVersicle/sevenSorrowsResponse/sevenSorrowsCollect.
